az_marley_wall.blurb: Marley Wall is a small sport crag at the far end of the Homestead, the limestone canyon of bolted lines along Highway 77 between Globe and Winkelman. It holds nine sport routes: one very easy line, a handful in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, and a couple of hard 5.13s, so it suits stronger climbers more than beginners. The wall faces south. Reaching it takes the longest hike of any wall in the canyon, roughly half an hour or more, so expect quieter conditions than the walls nearer the trailhead. A long rope and a good supply of quickdraws are worth bringing.

az_ravelin_the.blurb: The Ravelin is a compact sport crag among the Summit Crags near the top of Mount Lemmon in the Santa Catalina Mountains outside Tucson. Nine bolted routes sit here, nearly all between 5.10 and 5.12, with the most routes in the 5.11 range, so it is a place for climbers already comfortable on steeper, harder single pitches rather than newcomers. The cliff is short but obvious from the trail, and sits among bigger neighbours on the upper mountain. The high elevation makes it a cooler choice than the desert crags down the highway, and conditions are best from spring through fall.

az_right_wall.blurb: Right Wall is the final section of the Ricochet cliff, a short sport crag high on the San Francisco Peaks near Flagstaff at about 8,600 feet. It sits directly under the overlook at the end of the trail. All nine routes are bolted and run from 5.10 into 5.12, split evenly between the three grades, and the routes are tall. Because of the elevation it is a cool option for summer days. The cliff catches both sun and shade through the day, with the most shade in early morning and evening.

az_sixty_second_wall.blurb: Sixty Second Wall is a small southeast-facing crag in the Mid-Mountain zone of Mount Lemmon, right beside the San Pedro Vista pullout on the Catalina Highway. The walk from the car is only a minute or two, and the cliff looks out over a big view. Nine sport routes are here, mostly 5.10 to 5.11 with one 5.12 and a couple of easier lines, so it rewards intermediate and stronger climbers; there are few moderates. The zone around it is cool ponderosa forest, a good escape from the heat of the desert floor below.

az_hobo_house.blurb: Hobo House is a small, west-facing butte in Papago Park on the Tempe and Phoenix border, easy to spot from the Loop 202 freeway. It carries nine routes: mostly sport, a pair of top-ropes and one trad line, spanning an unusually wide range from 5.7 through the low 5.13s. The stone is dirty and uneven, though better than most of the rest of the park. The wall stays in shade until close to noon, then takes sun through the afternoon, so mornings suit hot months.

az_the_athenaeum_main_wall.blurb: The Athenaeum is the main wall of The Agora, a crag on the lower Catalina Highway on Mount Lemmon above Tucson. It has nine routes, seven bolted and two on gear, running from 5.7 to 5.11 with the bulk around 5.8. Most lines are long and begin steeply. The rock is decent but not perfect, so expect a few hollow spots. Each route has been cleaned thoroughly. The low elevation gives a Sonoran Desert setting that suits cooler months. To get here, drop in from the Solarium end of the crag and follow a brief trail.
az_the_athenaeum_main_wall.approach: Descend from the north end of The Agora through the Solarium ledges, then follow a short trail to the base of the wall.

az_glass_dome.blurb: Glass Dome is a small formation in the McDowell Mountains of the McDowell Sonoran Preserve near Scottsdale, just south of Tom's Thumb. Its smooth, glassy surface gave it the name. Routes are on the north, east and south faces, mostly traditional with one sport line and one top-rope, from about 5.6 up into the 5.11 range and a good share around 5.10. The walk starts at the Tom's Thumb trailhead and follows the trail south, then a short climbers' path.

az_loaf_the.blurb: The Loaf is a large granite formation split by an obvious central crack, on Little Granite Mountain in the northern McDowell Sonoran Preserve near Scottsdale. It is among the taller crags in the area and a good pick if you only have one day. Nine routes mix traditional and bolted lines, from an easy 5.4 through 5.9 with a cluster of 5.10s and one 5.11. The cliff faces east, so it takes sun from early to late morning and is shaded by afternoon, which is handy in warm weather. Few climbers show up on weekday mornings.
az_loaf_the.approach: From the trailhead lot, follow the Granite Mountain Loop Trail north and west until the large cracked formation appears beside the trail, then take the worn use path to its base.

_conflicts.az_right_wall: Stored rock is rhyolite; the Ricochet crag page (https://mountainproject.com/area/120555573/ricochet) calls the whole cliff andesite/dacite, and the Right Wall page (https://www.mountainproject.com/area/120555782/right-wall) gives no rock type. Rock left unchanged, not named in the blurb.
_conflicts.az_glass_dome: Stored rock is granite; https://mountainproject.com/area/116543726/glass-dome describes the dome as fine-grained aplite at the boundary with Pinnacle Peak granite. Left unchanged, not named in the blurb.
